# dead-code-pruner

> Conservative multi-language dead-code elimination for feature-flag cleanup, boolean constant folding, and static-analysis-driven source cleanup.

dead-code-pruner uses tree-sitter to replace permanently true/false feature flags with literals, simplify boolean expressions, eliminate dead if-branches, inline constant-return methods, and remove provably-unused methods and fields in a 3-phase iterative pipeline until convergence. It targets dead code cleanup for Java, Kotlin (Android / JVM server), Go server, Swift iOS, and Dart/Flutter projects while preserving dynamic framework entry points.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/OldJii/dead-code-pruner/blob/main/README.md): Pipeline, configuration, architecture, and usage
- [pruner.example.yaml](https://github.com/OldJii/dead-code-pruner/blob/main/pruner.example.yaml): Example config

## Pipeline

**Phase 1** — Constant folding + local propagation + boolean simplification + unreachable code removal (steps 1–4, loops until stable)
**Phase 2** — Constant-return method inlining (boolean + non-boolean) + cascade simplification
**Phase 3** — Dead method and unused field cleanup + cascade simplification + empty class/file removal

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp pruner.example.yaml pruner.yaml
python3 -m pruner /path/to/project --dry-run
python3 -m pruner /path/to/project
```

## Key facts

- **Languages**: Java, Kotlin, Go, Swift, Dart (5 ecosystems)
- **Engine**: tree-sitter AST
- **Dependencies**: Python 3.10+, tree-sitter grammars, PyYAML
- **Safety**: annotated-member aware, static-import and inheritance aware, dynamic XML/selector aware, multi-declaration safe, per-file AST rollback
- **Performance**: unified parallel project scan, compact indexes, incremental rescans, and in-place progress updates for long-running stages
- **License**: MIT
